El-Erian, cited the latest October 2026 U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data in a\u0026nbsp;\u003ca class=\"st-link-external\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer nofollow\" href=\"https://x.com/elerianm/status/2125588551660151197\"\u003epost\u003c/a\u003e on X and other economic parameters to point out that markets will now feel that a rate hike on Dec. 9 “is essentially a done deal.”\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 class=\"st-heading-2\"\u003eWhat Does The Data Suggest?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003eOctober’s PCE data released by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis showed that headline inflation rose to 3.8% year-over-year and increased 0.3% month-over-month, largely in line with market expectations. Core PCE climbed to 3.3% year-over-year, ahead of Street expectations of 3.2%.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eConsumer personal spending increased 0.3% month-over-month, slightly below the 0.4% forecast.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eReal gross domestic product increased at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis, beating market expectations of 3.5% and marking a strong upward revision from the initial advance estimate of 3.4%.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eMeanwhile, spot dollar is up to 103.714. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yields were trading at 4.864% at the time of writing, while 30-year yields were at 5.254%.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eEconomist Robin Brooks, a Senior Fellow at The Brookings Institution and a former chief FX strategist and managing director at Goldman Sachs, said that the rising dollar implies “very worrying” signals about global financial conditions,\u0026nbsp;\u003cbr\u003ewhich are tightening in a disorderly and rapid manner.”\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIn a\u0026nbsp;\u003ca class=\"st-link-external\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer nofollow\" href=\"https://x.com/robin_j_brooks/status/2125615986946490866\"\u003epost\u003c/a\u003e on X, he said, “All this originates from the Fed, whose ill-advised hikes in the face of tumbling oil prices are pushing up real rates…”\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 class=\"st-heading-2\"\u003eCan A Rate Hike Squeeze Markets?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003eJackson noted in a\u0026nbsp;\u003ca class=\"st-link-external\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer nofollow\" href=\"https://x.com/ericjackson/status/2125621817704435915\"\u003epost\u003c/a\u003e on X that while Fed Governor Chris Waller championed a 50-basis-point rate hike in December, key market data was pointing toward a different outcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eHe highlighted that the 10-year Treasury yield was trading around 4.80%, down from its 5% highs earlier this month, while oil prices had also declined, even though the Iran war was still ongoing.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e“What if the bond and commodity markets are seeing something the Fed isn't?
